name: Mactan Cebu International Airport
before:
The second busiest airport in the Philippines and the main gateway to the Central Visayas, on Mactan island in Lapu-Lapu City.

The quality is genuinely high for its size. Airports Council International named it the best airport in the Asia-Pacific region in the 5 to 15 million passenger category in both 2024 and 2025, and it was named Asia's airport of the year at the 2025 Travel Trade Excellence Awards.

There are two passenger terminals and the split is straightforward. Terminal 1, built in 1990, is now the domestic terminal, with six jet bridges and twelve remote stands. Terminal 2 took over international flights. A third terminal has been planned since 2019.

It is a hub for Philippine Airlines and an operating base for Cebu Pacific, Philippines AirAsia and Sunlight Air.

The airport opened on 27 April 1966 and is operated by Aboitiz InfraCapital.
